 Judgment

Dated this the 15th day of June 2020 This appeal is filed by the Food Inspector, Kannur Municipality against the acquittal order passed by the Judicial First Class Magistrate I, Kannur in C.C. No.47/2001.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate I, Kannur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The respondents, herein, are the accused in the above case.
(Hereinafter the parties are mentioned by their rank before the trial court).

2. The Food Inspector, Kannur filed a complaint against the respondents/accused for prosecuting them under Sections 16(1-A)(i) r/w Section 2(ia) (a)(j) & (m) and Section 7(1) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954 and Rule 29 and Rule 5 Appendix B-A-16-06 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules 1955.
(hereinafter referred to as the PFA Act & Rules respectively).
3. The case of the complaint, in brief, is that the Food Inspector inspected the hotel by name "Wheat House" running at door No.206, Civil Station Road, Kannur on 26.8.1997 at about 4.50 p.m.
After introducing himself as the Food Inspector he purchased one bottle of Tomato Sauce from a set of six bottles.
After complying the legal formalities, he took a sample from the tomato sauce and prepared a mahassar.
Thereafter, according to the Food inspector, he forwarded one set of samples for getting an expert opinion.
The Public Analyst reported that the sample does not conform to the standards prescribed in the tomato sauce under the PFA Rules.
Hence the complaint.
4. To substantiate the case, PW1 to PW4 were examined on the side of the complainant.
Exts.P1 to P20 are the exhibits marked by the prosecution.
One witness was examined as DW1 on the side of the defence, who is none other than the first accused.
Ext.D1 is also marked on the side of the defence.
On going though the evidence and documents, the trial court found that the accused has not committed the offences and all the accused persons are acquitted under Section 248(1) Cr.P.C.
Aggrieved by the above acquittal order, this Criminal Appeal is filed.
5. The point for consideration is whether the complainant was able to prove the offences alleged against the respondents/accused under the provisions of PFA Act and Rules.

6. Heard the learned Public Prosecutor and the counsel for the accused.
7.
The trial court acquitted the accused mainly for the following ground.

"From the light of the appreciation entered above, myself fully satisfied and convinced that PW1 had failed to establish the material fact that the Tomato sauce which he had taken was actually stored and kept in the storeroom which is attached to the kitchen is meant for either for sale as such or kept it for making any food articles with a view to either distribute the same among the customers or to sell the same."

sentences.text: I reserve my comments about the finding of the learned magistrate.
Since the accused is entitled for an acquittal on another ground, I think the ground on which the accused was acquitted need not be considered.

A Division Bench of this Court in Rasheed N.K. Vs. Food Inspector, Thalassery and another (2016 (2) KLT 390) held that the prosecution under the PFA Act 1954 will not lie unless the laboratory for the analysis by Public Analysts is not defined and the method of analysis are also defined under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and Section 23 (1-A) (hh) of the PFA Act.

entities.text: Rasheed N.K. Vs. Food Inspector, Thalassery and another (2016 (2) KLT 390)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As on the date of Ext.P9 analysis report, which is relied on by the prosecution, in this case, the laboratories for analysis by the Public analysts and the method of analysis are not notified in accordance to Section 23(1-A) (ee) and Section 23(1-A) (hh)of the PFA Act.

Section 23(1) of the PFA Act says that the Central Government may, after consultation with the Committee and after previous publication, in the official gazette make Rules to carry out the provisions of this Act.

Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh)
says that, in particular and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power such Rules may provide for all or any of the following matters namely-"defining the laboratories where samples of article of food for adulterants may be analyzed by public analysts under this "Act and defining the method of analysis".
There is no rules framed in accordance to Section 23 (1) (a)(ee) and (hh) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
In such circumstances, the prosecution in this case based on Ext.P9 form No.3 report dated 22.9.1997 is unsustainable.
Therefore, the prosecution itself is not maintainable in this case.
Hence, this appeal is dismissed confirming the acquittal order passed by the trial court.

Sd/-
P.V.KUNHIKRISHNAN JUDGE al/-+
